_comment: FRENCH ad read on a preset timbre, with natural-language delivery direction. This is the workflow the brief means by 'test this hardest, including French' - Qwen3-TTS publishes a French WER of 2.858, the best of any open model surveyed, and this graph is how that gets verified against our own copy rather than against a paper.
_instruct: The `instruct` field is the differentiator versus every other model in this stack: delivery is directed in plain language rather than through an exaggeration slider. Write it as you would brief a voice actor - 'warm, unhurried, like explaining to a neighbour' - and it applies tone, pace and emotion. Leave it empty for a neutral read.
_speakers: Nine presets: Aiden, Dylan, Eric, Ono_anna, Ryan, Serena, Sohee, Uncle_fu, Vivian. Each has a native language and can speak any of the ten supported; quality is best in its native one. None is natively French, so for francophone-facing work A/B this against qwen-clone.json with a real French reference - a cloned native speaker will usually beat a preset speaking out of its native language.
_language: Set `language` explicitly rather than leaving it on Auto whenever the target language is known. Auto adapts from the text, and a French script with an English brand name in it can tip the detector.

inputs.text: Nos equipes posent votre plancher en deux jours, pas en deux semaines. Chene blanc d'ingenierie, fini huile mat, en stock a notre entrepot de Mississauga.
inputs.speaker: Serena
inputs.instruct: Chaleureuse et posee, comme si vous expliquiez a un voisin. Pas de ton publicitaire.
